subtype: Approach: giving up after one bad fall [Pitfall]
passage: It had rained an hour before, and the road by the park was slick. Sharmila pedalled hard, hit a patch of mud and slid onto her elbow. Her friend Sachin ran over and lifted the cycle. Her sleeve was torn and her elbow scraped. "Never again," she said. "Cycling is too dangerous." Sachin frowned. "It was the mud. Try tomorrow?" Sharmila shook her head and walked the cycle home. The next week, Sachin and the other kids rode to the lake together, laughing, and Sharmila watched them from the balcony with her chin on her hands.

qa.a: Sharmila slid on a patch of mud.

qa.q: What was Sharmila feeling when she said cycling is too dangerous?
qa.a: Sharmila was shaken and frightened; the torn sleeve and scraped elbow made cycling feel unsafe. 😔

qa.q: What alternative approach could Sharmila use, and why might it help?
qa.a: Sharmila could try again on a dry day in a quiet place with a helmet and a friend nearby. A safer setting can rebuild confidence without ignoring the fall.

qa.q: How might Sachin see her decision to stop?
qa.a: Sachin thought the mud was the problem and suggested trying tomorrow, so Sachin probably feels sorry to see a friend miss the rides.

grounding: After scraping her elbow, a child declares cycling too dangerous and gives up, which keeps her safe from falls but also from the joy of riding with friends.

subtype: Approach: giving up after one bad fall [Pitfall]
passage:
Vidya scraped her elbow on the colony road one Sunday and announced at dinner that cycling was "too dangerous for normal people." The pink cycle went behind the water tank. Two weeks later, the girls from her building planned an evening ride to the ice-cream cart two lanes away. Trisha knocked on the door. "Coming? You can ride right behind me."
"I don't ride any more," Vidya said, arms folded.
From the window she watched them go, bells ringing, Trisha waving back. She told herself she didn't care. Then she went to her room and shut the door harder than she meant to. The elbow had healed days ago.

qa.q: Where did the pink cycle go after Vidya's fall?
qa.a: The pink cycle went behind the water tank.

qa.q: What does the way Vidya shuts her door suggest she was feeling?
qa.a: She was hurt and left out, and angry with herself, even while she told herself she didn't care.

qa.q: What would you change first to help Vidya ride again?
qa.a: She could start with a short, slow ride with Trisha on the quiet side of the building, so the fear shrinks without another big fall.

qa.q: How does Vidya's refusal look to Trisha?
qa.a: Trisha offers to ride right beside her, so she probably feels puzzled and a bit sad that her friend stays behind.

grounding: It shows a child who stops cycling after one scrape and, while staying safe from falls, misses a fun ride with friends.

subtype: Approach: giving up after one bad fall [Pitfall]
passage:
"Vinita, everyone's going to the lake path. Get your cycle."
"No, Vijay bhaiya. I'm never riding again."
"Because of one fall?"
"Look at my elbow! It bled. Cycles are dangerous."
"It was a scrape. It's nearly healed."
"I could fall again and break my arm."
"So you'll walk behind us?"
"I'm not coming at all."
That evening Vijay came back pink-cheeked.
"We saw a heron! Then everyone raced down the slope. Best ride ever."
"I don't care."
"Then why did you ask Mummy three times where we went?"
"Because. Go away."
She turned the pages of her book very fast, not reading a word.

qa.q: What did Vijay and the others see at the lake path?
How was Vinita feeling when she said "I don't care"?
qa.a: She was left out and jealous of the fun, and probably still scared, so she covered it by sounding cross.

qa.q: What else could Vinita try instead of stopping altogether?
qa.a: She could ride only the flat part of the path with Vijay beside her, so she stays careful but is still part of the outing.

qa.q: How does Vinita's decision look to Vijay?
qa.a: Vijay thinks one scrape is a small reason to miss out, and he can tell she does care from her questions.

grounding: It shows a child who refuses to ride after scraping her elbow, avoiding falls but missing the joy of riding together.
